---
title: "Installation"
---

## Python Environment

CodeBook Lab supports Python 3.10 and newer. A virtual environment keeps package dependencies separate from the rest of your system.

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install codebook-lab
```

If you plan to score textbox annotations, install the optional textbox dependencies:

```bash
python -m pip install "codebook-lab[textbox]"
```

Every textbox metric needs these extras: normalized Levenshtein similarity (`python-Levenshtein`), BLEU (`nltk`), ROUGE (`rouge-score`), embedding cosine similarity (`sentence-transformers`) and BERTScore (`bert-score`, `torch`). Without them, textbox fields are still generated and get a percentage-agreement score, but their similarity metrics are left blank and `classification_reports.txt` lists the missing packages. The extras include PyTorch, so they are a large download. Checkbox, dropdown, Likert and span metrics need nothing extra.

## Ollama

CodeBook Lab runs models through [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download), which you install separately. Once it is installed, you don't need to start it or download models yourself:

- **Starting the server.** If Ollama isn't running, each run starts it in the background with `ollama serve`. This only happens for a server on the default local address (`http://127.0.0.1:11434`). To use Ollama on another machine, set the `OLLAMA_HOST` environment variable to its address and start that server yourself.
- **Downloading models.** `run_experiment()` calls `ollama pull` for the model before every run. For a model you already have, this only checks for updates, which is usually quick but needs an internet connection: if the pull fails, the run stops with an error. Pass `pull_model=False` (or `pull_models=False` for a sweep) to skip the check, for example when working offline or to keep a model version fixed during a benchmark.

```python
from codebook_lab import ExperimentSpec, run_experiment

result = run_experiment(
    ExperimentSpec(
        task="policy-sentiment",
        model="gemma3:270m",
        country_iso_code="IRL",
    )
)
```

`country_iso_code` is the three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code for where the computation physically runs, such as `IRL`, `USA` or `DEU`. CodeCarbon uses it to look up the electricity grid's carbon intensity when converting energy use to emissions. It defaults to `USA`, so set it whenever you run elsewhere, or the emissions estimates will be wrong. Energy use itself is measured on your machine and does not depend on this setting.

## Development Install

For package development, clone the repository and install it in editable mode:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/LorcanMcLaren/codebook-lab.git
cd codebook-lab
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```

Use `python -m pip install -e ".[all,dev]"` if you also want the optional textbox metric dependencies in the development environment.
